extraction.name: Visual Question Answering: Datasets, Algorithms, and Future Challenges
extraction.description: This paper is a review of visual question answering (VQA) that critically examines existing VQA datasets, evaluation metrics, and algorithms. It discusses the strengths and weaknesses of publicly released VQA datasets and analyzes limitations such as dataset bias and evaluation challenges.
extraction.creator: Kushal Kafle (Rochester Institute of Technology); Christopher Kanan (Rochester Institute of Technology)
extraction.citeAs: Kushal Kafle and Christopher Kanan. Visual Question Answering: Datasets, Algorithms, and Future Challenges. arXiv:1610.01465v4, 2017.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: This review describes multiple VQA datasets as being assembled from existing image datasets and by collecting human-generated questions and answers. It states that COCO-QA created QA pairs from COCO image captions using an NLP algorithm; COCO-VQA used Amazon Mechanical Turk workers to generate questions and a separate pool of workers to generate answers for COCO images; FM-IQA contains human generated questions and answers and was originally collected in Chinese; Visual Genome used two data collection modes, free-form questions and region-specific prompting for annotators; and Visual7W is a subset of Visual Genome.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis; Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The review states that DAQUAR is based on images from the NYU-DepthV2 Dataset; COCO-QA uses COCO image captions; COCO-VQA contains real images from COCO and abstract cartoon images; FM-IQA is based on COCO; Visual Genome consists of images that occur in both YFCC100M and COCO; and Visual7W is a subset of Visual Genome containing images also present in COCO.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: COCO-VQA consists of three questions per image, with ten answers per question; Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) workers were employed to generate questions for each image by being asked to "Stump a smart robot," and a separate pool of workers were hired to generate the answers to the questions. Visual Genome used two distinct modes of data collection: in the free-form method, annotators were free to ask any question about an image, and in the region-specific method, workers were prompted to ask questions about specific image regions using descriptive bounding-box annotations. Visual7W collected plausible answers by prompting annotators to answer the question without seeing the image.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For COCO-VQA, the multiple answers per question are used in the consensus-based evaluation metric for the dataset; the Correct Answer is the most frequent answer given by the ten annotators.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Amazon Mechanical Turk workers; annotators for SYNTH-VQA spanned different age, gender, and races
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The authors discuss that many current VQA datasets contain exploitable biases, including language biases that allow questions to be answered without using the image; COCO-VQA has answer distribution bias such as yes/no answers spanning about 38% of all questions and almost 59% of them being answered with yes; DAQUAR contains exclusively indoor scenes, constraining question variety
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Current VQA benchmarks are not sufficient to evaluate whether a system is capable of robust image understanding; many datasets can be accurately answered without using the image due to language biases; COCO-QA contains awkwardly phrased, grammatically incorrect, and sometimes unintelligible questions due to flaws in automatic QA generation; DAQUAR is too small to successfully train and evaluate more complex models and contains only indoor scenes; COCO-VQA contains many subjective, opinion-seeking, explanatory, or descriptive questions that do not have a single objective answer; existing evaluation metrics are problematic, especially for multi-word answers, and multiple-choice evaluation can undermine VQA by allowing systems to peek at the correct answer
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper states that VQA could aid blind and visually impaired individuals by enabling them to get information about images on the web and in the real world; it could improve human-computer interaction as a natural way to query visual content; it could also be used for image retrieval without metadata or tags
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The human models are the same as those used in [41], and they contain deformable limbs and eight different facial expressions. The models also span different age, gender, and races to provide variation in appearance.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: training and evaluation of visual question answering systems; aid to blind and visually impaired individuals for getting information about images; improving human-computer interaction as a natural way to query visual content; image retrieval without using image metadata or tags; component of a Visual Turing Test for image understanding
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For the multiple-choice format of The VQA Dataset, the same QA pairs were post-collection transformed by adding 18 answer choices composed of the correct answer, three plausible answers collected from annotators without looking at the image, the top ten most popular answers in the dataset, and random correct answers from other questions.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: In COCO-QA, QA pairs are automatically derived from COCO captions using an NLP algorithm; longer sentences are broken into smaller chunks for ease of processing.
